title: Stop Ordering AI Takeout  A Cookbook for Winning When You Build In House - Jan Siml
talk_summary: A business-side case study arguing that in-house AI should target one narrow, high-value workflow with clear dollar attribution rather than chasing benchmarks or multi-agent complexity.

takeaways.what_they_do: They ran the same workflow on a small/cheap model and a large model and found only cost and offline eval scores changed, not the business outcome, so they defaulted to the cheap model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When we changed the models from normal to the miniseries and back, the only thing that changed were the costs and the evils.
takeaways.numbers: claims o3 is ~60x more expensive and an order of magnitude slower than 4.1-mini

takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument the full funnel to a dollar-based value event and prioritize by that instead of F1/NDCG, treating evals as smoke alarms only.
takeaways.evidence_quote: offline evals never sign a contract. Nobody at the board meeting asks for your F1 score

takeaways.what_they_do: They stopped waiting for users to ask and pushed daily digests of what needs attention, keeping a chat UI only as fallback for unplanned tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the best UI is the one you never need to use
takeaways.numbers: proactive system had 20 points higher NPS and an order of magnitude higher engagement vs chat app

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately kept the first workflow simple and avoided agentic/multi-agent designs, going deep on one job instead of broad coverage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you stay focused, you can keep things very simple and avoid anything agentic.
